JSON: Name: igfbp7_stat3_la_dkd_pipeline Title: Preclinical evaluation of levomefolic acid inhibition of IGFBP7-mediated acetylated-STAT3 dimerization to restore mitochondrial fatty-acid oxidation and reduce progression of diabetic kidney disease Short Hypothesis: Pharmacologic inhibition of IGFBP7 with levomefolic acid reduces acetylated-STAT3 dimerization in renal tubular epithelial cells, thereby restoring PGC-1α–dependent mitochondrial fatty-acid oxidation, decreasing tubular lipid accumulation and interstitial fibrosis, and lowering albuminuria in diabetic mouse models. Related Work: Previous studies identify IGFBP7 as an upregulated secreted protein in early diabetic kidney disease (DKD) and a biomarker of renal tubular stress; separate literature implicates impaired mitochondrial fatty-acid oxidation (FAO) in proximal tubular cells as a driver of lipotoxicity and renal fibrosis. STAT3 is a known regulator whose acetylation promotes dimer stability and nuclear activity; STAT3 activation has been linked to suppression of PGC-1α and mitochondrial dysfunction. Prior interventions have targeted individual nodes (epigenetic regulators of transcription, AMPK/PGC-1α activation, or STAT3 phosphorylation) but have not demonstrated a tubular-epithelial-secreted-protein → STAT3 acetylation → PGC-1α → FAO causal chain with a small-molecule antagonist. Limitations of existing approaches include limited cell-type specificity, incomplete rescue of FAO, overreliance on correlative human biomarker studies, a paucity of validated small molecules that disrupt extracellular IGFBP7 interactions, and insufficient translational pharmacology data on candidates with acceptable toxicity profiles. Abstract: Diabetic kidney disease progression is driven by tubular mitochondrial metabolic failure, lipid accumulation, interstitial fibrosis, and ensuing glomerular damage. This pipeline tests whether targeting the tubular-secreted protein IGFBP7 can reverse these processes by preventing STAT3 acetylation-dependent dimerization and restoring PGC-1α–driven mitochondrial fatty-acid oxidation (FAO). We propose a preclinical program combining in vitro mechanistic assays, multi-omic profiling, and in vivo diabetic mouse models to evaluate levomefolic acid (LA) as a direct IGFBP7 antagonist. Key contributions are: (1) biochemical and cellular validation of LA binding to IGFBP7 and disruption of the IGFBP7–STAT3 interaction; (2) demonstration that LA treatment restores FAO and PGC-1α activity in renal tubular cells and organoids; and (3) proof-of-concept that systemic LA reduces tubular lipid deposition, interstitial fibrosis, and albuminuria in type 1 and type 2 diabetic mouse models, with concurrent safety profiling. Expected outcomes include mechanistic validation of the IGFBP7–STAT3–PGC-1α axis as a therapeutic target for DKD and preclinical efficacy/safety data to inform translation. Experiments: 1) In vitro mechanistic studies (cell lines and primary cells): cell types: human HK2, primary human renal TECs, mouse mTECs, MPC5 podocytes. Conditions: normal glucose (5.6 mM), high glucose (30 mM), ± palmitic acid (200 μM). Interventions: vehicle, graded LA concentrations (0.1, 0.5, 1, 5 μM), IGFBP7 siRNA, STAT3 siRNA, STAT3 mutants (K685R, K4Q, Y705A), PGC-1α overexpression, etomoxir (FAO inhibitor, 40 μM) as mechanistic control. Readouts: co-immunoprecipitation IGFBP7–STAT3, STAT3 acetylation (K685) and phosphorylation (Y705) by western blot, STAT3 dimerization (native PAGE/Co-IP), ubiquitination and MDM2 interaction assays, PGC-1α mRNA/protein and promoter luciferase, mitochondrial OCR (Seahorse ATP-linked, maximal respiration, spare capacity), FAO flux (14C-palmitate oxidation or equivalent), Oil Red O lipid quantification, secreted TGF-β1/CTGF (ELISA). Comparisons: LA vs vehicle; LA vs IGFBP7 siRNA; LA + etomoxir vs LA alone; STAT3 mutant rescue. N≥3 biological replicates per condition. 2) Biophysical validation: SPR and CETSA for LA–IGFBP7 and IGFBP7–STAT3 interactions; KD determination; thermal shift ΔTm. 3) Ex vivo organoid assays: kidney organoids from FF and IGFBP7-cKO mice exposed to HG ± LA (1 μM); readouts: fibrotic markers by IF, OCR, and RNA-seq. 4) In vivo efficacy and mechanism: mouse cohorts: C57BL/6 STZ-induced type 1 DKD (50 mg/kg x 5); HFD+low-dose STZ and db/db for type 2 DKD; genetic models: IGFBP7 tubular conditional KO (ksp-cre), podocyte cKO (nphs1-cre), IGFBP7 overexpression transgenic, STAT3 tubular cKO. Treatment arms: vehicle, LA low/med/high doses (0.5, 2.5, 10 mg/kg weekly IP or oral as PK supports), STAT3 AAV knockdown, etomoxir control, and combinations. N=8-12 per group (power calculation for UACR effect size 30%, α=0.05, β=0.8). Timeline: 24 weeks for chronic models; interim 10-week cohorts for STZ acute progression. Endpoints: urinary albumin/creatinine ratio (UACR), serum creatinine, transcutaneous FITC-sinistrin GFR, histological fibrosis area (Masson % area), glomerular basement membrane thickness and foot process effacement (TEM), renal lipidomics (absolute quantification), renal RNA-seq for FAO and inflammatory pathways, immunoblot for STAT3 acetylation/dimerization and PGC-1α, mitochondrial OCR in isolated tubules, liver/heart toxicity panels (ALT/AST, histology). 5) Comparative and ablation studies: (a) LA vs IGFBP7 genetic KO vs STAT3 knockdown to test pathway specificity; (b) LA dose-response and PK/PD correlation with renal IGFBP7 occupancy; (c) LA + AMPK activator (e.g., AICAR) and LA + NF-κB inhibitor (BAY11-7082) arms to test additive effects; (d) use of STAT3 K685R knock-in or AAV-delivered mutants in TECs to test acetylation dependence. Statistical analysis: ANOVA with Tukey post hoc or mixed-effects models for longitudinal data; multiple testing correction for omics (FDR<0.05). Risk Factors and Limitations: Technical failure modes: LA may not sufficiently disrupt IGFBP7–STAT3 interaction in vivo due to binding affinity, bioavailability, or renal delivery limitations; off-target binding of LA may confound mechanistic readouts; redundancy or compensation via STAT family members or parallel fibrotic pathways could mask effects. Data and model limitations: mouse DKD models incompletely recapitulate human disease heterogeneity; genetic KO/overexpression models may introduce developmental compensation; primary human TEC variability and limited biopsy sample sizes may bias translational conclusions. Measurement and evaluation biases: reliance on surrogate markers (UACR, histology) may not predict long-term function; omics associations may be confounded by cell-type composition changes. Scalability and resources: repeated chronic dosing and multi-omic analyses are resource-intensive; high-throughput biophysical assays and adequate animal group sizes require substantial funding and specialized equipment. Generalization limits: efficacy in rodents may not translate to humans due to species differences in IGFBP7 biology, STAT3 regulation, and folate metabolism; potential long-term safety risks of systemic LA exposure are undercharacterized, especially at therapeutic doses required for target engagement.
